title: Matched TEA/TEOA benchmark
question: Test whether changing the amine from TEOA to TEA alone alters CO/H2 distribution in the P01 Co-bpy/g-C3N4 platform under intentionally unmatched conditions to maximize donor contrast.
measurements: GC-detected CO amount; GC-detected H2 amount; CO/H2 ratio or selectivity descriptor; Qualitative note of visible instability or precipitation after reaction
limitations: This design wrongly treats donor substitution as a single-variable test even though amine identity can alter medium composition, proton behavior, and CO2 interactions. It does not isolate mechanism and weakly controls background artifacts.

title: Matched donor-specific necessity and background controls
question: Test whether any TEA versus TEOA CO/H2 difference persists only in the complete photocatalytic formulation after symmetric light, gas-feed, and cobalt-necessity controls for both donors.
measurements: GC-detected CO amount; GC-detected H2 amount; CO/H2 product ratio or selectivity metric calculated from the same GC dataset; Whether each donor-matched control is above, near, or below blank/detection background; Optional note of visible precipitation or color change as a non-decisive covariate
limitations: This card tests assay validity and donor dependence under one matched formulation but does not isolate why donors differ. No-cobalt omission does not separately test ligand or absorber necessity. Equal nominal conditions do not guarantee equal pH, donor consumption, or active-species population, so mechanistic interpretation remains bounded.

title: Donor amount series
question: Test whether any TEA/TEOA difference persists across donor loadings by sweeping donor amount and reading selectivity trends, assuming amount and identity can be merged into one practical causal factor.
measurements: GC-detected CO amount; GC-detected H2 amount; CO/H2 ratio across the four groups; Simple trend direction with donor amount
limitations: This combines donor identity and medium perturbation issues and overinterprets nominally matched additions as chemically matched conditions. Two-point amount sampling can miss nonmonotonic behavior and cannot isolate mechanism.

title: TEA versus TEOA donor-side quenching comparison in the verified P01 baseline matrix
question: Test whether replacing TEOA with TEA changes upstream photoredox observables in a verified P01 baseline formulation under strictly matched nonreactive measurement conditions, as a descriptive covariate for any donor-dependent CO/H2 shift without claiming catalytic causation.
measurements: Steady-state fluorescence intensity of the absorber-containing sample under matched excitation; Optional fluorescence lifetime proxy only if available and if scattering permits meaningful extraction; UV-vis absorbance or difference spectra before and after donor addition or short irradiation exposure; Background absorbance and scattering from donor, solvent matrix, and cobalt-containing mixtures; Empirical quenching trend summaries for cobalt-free and cobalt-containing matrices
limitations: This is characterization, not a catalytic readout. In a g-C3N4-containing or otherwise scattering matrix, fluorescence and UV-vis assignments can be compromised by adsorption, inner-filter effects, and turbidity. Even with cobalt-free controls, the experiment cannot identify the turnover-relevant intermediate or prove that a donor-dependent optical change causes a donor-dependent CO/H2 shift. Transfer from EV053, EV065, GX007, and EV011 is methodological and donor-chemistry based, not direct proof for the exact P01 catalytic manifold.

title: Near-operando cobalt-state comparison under TEOA and TEA
question: Assess whether TEA and TEOA correlate with different cobalt-associated oxidation or coordination signatures in the P01-like system under matched conditions, while keeping inference descriptive unless donor-linked differences survive donor-matched backgrounds and matched timing.
measurements: Cobalt-associated spectral signatures consistent with oxidation-state or coordination-environment change; Donor-matched difference spectra between pre-illumination and illuminated-state samples; Donor-matched cobalt-free background spectra before and after the same illumination protocol; If feasible, a second independent spectral readout on the same matched sample set
limitations: Assignments in a mixed support-plus-molecular matrix remain uncertain, and before-versus-illuminated comparisons are time-coupled rather than isolated causal tests. This card addresses state correlation under matched donors, not full active-species identification or causal pathway separation.

title: 13CO2 origin check for CO under matched TEOA and TEA conditions
question: Determine whether CO detected in the matched donor comparison is CO2-derived under both donor identities, protecting the TEA/TEOA selectivity comparison against donor-specific carbon artifacts or background CO formation.
measurements: GC-MS isotopic pattern for CO under 13CO2 and under unlabeled CO2 references; CO and H2 amounts from the same matched runs to preserve donor-comparison context; Signals in donor-matched catalyst-omission controls to bound analytical or background CO contributions; Repeat-injection or repeat-run consistency for low-signal labeled CO assignment if signal is near detection limit
limitations: This card verifies product origin and bounds catalyst dependence of labeled CO detection; it does not resolve whether donor effects arise from photophysics, proton management, medium composition, or cobalt-state changes. Before/after agreement in product origin cannot by itself establish the operating-state mechanism.

title: Matched donor quenching in P01
question: Test whether replacing TEOA with TEA changes absorber-side quenching or bleaching behavior in the primary Co-bpy/g-C3N4 platform while other formulation elements are held fixed.
measurements: Steady-state emission intensity or Stern-Volmer-type response of the absorber-containing sample; UV-vis absorbance changes or bleaching trajectories under matched illumination; Background absorbance and scattering from donor-containing blanks and no-cobalt references; Replicate-to-replicate variance sufficient to judge whether TEA and TEOA differences exceed optical background drift; If filtrates are used, note that filtrate signals cannot establish the dominant operating state of suspended g-C3N4-bound species
limitations: Steady-state optical changes can indicate donor-dependent quenching or bleaching but cannot by themselves assign the reduced cobalt species, quantify electron flux into catalysis, or prove causation for CO/H2 selectivity. Support effects in P01 may make absorber and cobalt contributions overlap. No-cobalt references do not recreate the full catalytic manifold. If multiple factors such as donor identity and pH drift co-vary, causal attribution remains limited.

title: Transient reduced-state comparison
question: Determine whether TEA and TEOA produce different transient amplitudes or decay kinetics in the P01 cobalt-containing formulation, while bounding interpretation if donor substitution also changes bulk medium or interfacial properties.
measurements: Transient absorption or analogous pump-probe amplitude at selected probe wavelengths; Decay kinetics or characteristic lifetimes in reproducible time windows; Ground-state bleach recovery if observable; Dark and no-donor background traces for artifact detection; No-cobalt reference traces to separate cobalt-associated changes from absorber or support-side dynamics; Bulk covariates for each donor condition, including pH or comparable acidity-basicity readout, optical density or scattering proxy, and suspension-handling notes; Assignment confidence statement distinguishing descriptive donor-sensitive transients from specifically assigned cobalt intermediates
limitations: Species assignment in a heterogeneous supported system is provisional, and transient differences do not uniquely prove electron flow into a specific cobalt intermediate. Donor substitution can co-vary pH, viscosity, ionic environment, adsorption, and suspension stability, so even a clear transient difference may reflect combined effects. No-cobalt controls help bound interpretation but do not recreate the same interfacial environment as cobalt-containing samples.

title: Supplementary P02 quenching transfer
question: Use the more chemically defined homogeneous cobalt/Ru platform P02 as a supplementary test of whether TEA versus TEOA changes donor-side quenching behavior when support effects are minimized.
measurements: Photosensitizer emission intensity and quenching response versus donor condition; Stern-Volmer-type slopes or other relative quenching metrics if the response is linear enough in the chosen range; UV-vis changes indicating donor- or cobalt-associated spectral perturbations; Blank and no-donor signals for baseline correction; Explicit note that quenching metrics in P02 cannot establish matched active chemistry or absolute electron flux in P01
limitations: This is a supplementary system, not the main inference target. Even a clean donor effect in P02 cannot prove that P01 shares the same mechanistic route because catalyst architecture, absorber identity, and support effects differ. Conversely, lack of a P02 effect does not eliminate a P01-specific donor influence. The experiment is best used for directional transfer, not quantitative mechanistic equivalence.

title: Matched TEA/TEOA photophysics-to-products correlation in the Co-bpy baseline, with optional homogeneous bridge
question: Test whether TEA-versus-TEOA substitution changes donor-side quenching or transient reduced-state observables in the same direction as any CO/H2 shift under otherwise matched conditions, while limiting inference to correlation-versus-discordance rather than causation.
measurements: CO amount and H2 amount from the same gas-analysis workflow; derived selectivity reported only as a transformation of measured products, not as a sole readout.; Emission intensity, spectrum, or lifetime changes of the light-absorbing component versus donor identity for matched mixtures or justified sub-mixtures; this reports quenching behavior but cannot alone identify the exact quencher or active intermediate.; Transient absorbance or equivalent time-resolved optical signal assigned to a reduced-state or charge-carrier proxy using references and backgrounds; this can indicate donor-dependent formation or persistence of a transient species but cannot by itself establish the active cobalt state.; Background product formation in cobalt-omission groups to bound donor, photosensitizer, or support contributions.; Documentation of sample-state comparability, including mixture composition, atmosphere, and illumination history for each measurement block.; If the optional bridge is used, the same classes of photophysical readouts and product measurements in P02 to test directionality transfer only.
limitations: This design tests correlation versus discordance, not causation. Even reproducible concordance between donor-side observables and CO/H2 does not exclude coupled changes in proton transfer, catalyst speciation, substrate binding, or other downstream chemistry. P01 support effects may decouple measured optical observables from the chemically active manifold. Cobalt-omission contrasts are necessity/background tests because omitting cobalt changes the reaction manifold. The optional P02 bridge improves photophysical interpretability but is not chemically identical to the Co-bpy/g-C3N4 target, so only bounded directionality transfer is justified.

title: Donor-radical detection under TEA versus TEOA substitution
question: Test whether replacing TEOA with TEA changes detectable donor-derived radical signatures under illumination in a matched cobalt comparison matrix. This is a bounded donor-side characterization experiment, not a direct product-causation test.
measurements: EPR or equivalent radical-detection spectra for illuminated, dark, and no-absorber donor-matched samples; Signal presence or absence relative to donor-matched backgrounds; Line shape and linewidth, explicitly noting possible viscosity or motion effects; Time-dependent growth and decay of radical-associated signals under matched irradiation and acquisition windows; If feasible, parallel absorber integrity check by optical spectroscopy
limitations: Radical trapping can perturb chemistry, and detected adducts may be secondary trapped products rather than the immediate quenching intermediate. TEA and TEOA can differ in viscosity and line broadening, so spectral differences are not automatically identity differences. If only a supplementary readable platform works, transfer back to the main catalytic platform remains limited. This experiment does not measure CO or H2.

title: Medium-normalized TEA vs TEOA with attribution controls
question: Test whether the TEA/TEOA CO/H2 difference in the P01 Co-bpy/g-C3N4 system persists after tighter recipe matching, while embedding internal attribution controls so any collapse of the difference is interpreted only as reduced compatibility with a strong medium-dominant explanation rather than proof of a specific proton-management mechanism.
measurements: Gas-phase CO amount versus time.; Gas-phase H2 amount versus time.; CO/H2 ratio or selectivity versus time calculated from jointly measured products.; Bulk pre- and post-run apparent pH of the liquid phase as a covariate only.; Qualitative notes on color change, precipitation, or phase separation as comparability checks only.; Analytical blank and calibration stability across the full sample set.
limitations: TEA and TEOA remain chemically nonequivalent even after composition normalization, so this card cannot isolate proton activity, dissolved CO2, viscosity, conductivity, and cobalt coordination effects from one another. The no-amine comparison also changes overall liquid composition and therefore tests functional necessity more than pure mechanistic causality. Product data alone cannot identify the active cobalt species or the dominant hidden variable behind any selectivity shift.

title: Isotope-sensitive operando signatures in TEA vs TEOA Co-bpy photocatalysis
question: Test whether TEA and TEOA produce different H/D-sensitive spectroscopic observables under one matched P01 configuration, consistent with different proton-coupled environments or hydrogen-containing states, while avoiding overclaim that isotope effects identify a unique intermediate.
measurements: Time-resolved spectra in predefined windows classified only as candidate hydrogen-coupled, CO2-derived, ligand-associated, support-associated, or background-sensitive features; Isotope-induced shifts, attenuation, or altered temporal evolution after H2O-to-D2O substitution within each donor condition; Difference spectra against dark, pre-illumination, and donor-free references to identify background or support-derived contributions; Replicate agreement of donor-dependent isotope responses across independently prepared samples; Parallel CO and H2 product amounts from matched runs to test co-occurrence with selectivity differences without equating correlation to cause
limitations: This card can test whether TEA and TEOA differ in isotope-sensitive observables under matched conditions, but it cannot uniquely identify intermediates, prove rate-determining roles, or isolate proton management from all donor-dependent medium changes. D2O substitution is itself a multi-property perturbation, and near-operando measurements may miss the true operating state.

title: CO2-associated donor speciation under matched P01 medium
question: Test whether TEA and TEOA create different detectable CO2-associated solution states in the P01 medium before illumination or after reaction-relevant equilibration, as a bounded indicator of donor-dependent local CO2/proton environment.
measurements: Difference IR spectra of CO2-equilibrated minus inert-equilibrated samples, tracking new or shifted bands attributable to donor- or bicarbonate/carbonate-associated environments.; NMR chemical-shift or line-shape changes for donor-containing samples before and after CO2 equilibration, if the medium permits interpretable spectra.; Background-reference spectra for no-amine and component-minus-one samples to bound non-donor contributions.; Simple covariates such as apparent acidity metric and conductivity; these can contextualize medium changes but cannot establish molecular identity on their own.; Replicate consistency of any donor-specific CO2-responsive signal; reproducibility is required before using the signal in later catalytic correlation studies.
limitations: This characterization is descriptive. A donor-specific CO2-responsive signal cannot by itself prove the catalytic intermediate, the active cobalt state, or the cause of CO/H2 selectivity. g-C3N4 and cobalt-bpy may contribute overlapping features, and dark-equilibrated samples may miss illumination-generated states. If donor identity changes pH, coordination, or suspension properties simultaneously, the comparison remains mechanistically mixed even when composition is nominally matched.

title: Amine omission and bounded inert-base replacement
question: Test whether amine presence is necessary in the P01 TEA/TEOA comparison and whether a tightly screened non-donor base can produce only limited medium-related shifts, without treating it as an amine surrogate or proof of proton-management causality.
measurements: CO amount or rate by the common gas-analysis workflow; H2 amount or rate by the same workflow; CO/H2 ratio or selectivity metric derived from paired CO and H2 data; Bulk acid-base descriptor before and after reaction if measurable in the chosen medium; Qualitative observations of precipitation, turbidity, color change, or phase separation as comparability checks
limitations: The replacement arm remains intrinsically limited because a non-donor base cannot reproduce sacrificial electron donation. Any observed rescue can also arise from coordination, ionic-strength, viscosity, or solvation changes. Failure to rescue does not exclude proton-management contributions. Bulk acid-base descriptors in MeCN/H2O may not represent local proton delivery. This card therefore tests necessity plus bounded medium sensitivity, not full causal separation.

title: TEA/TEOA water-fraction crossover map in the P01 baseline
question: Test whether the TEA-versus-TEOA CO/H2 difference depends strongly on MeCN/H2O composition, consistent with donor effects arising largely from proton management and local CO2/medium properties rather than donor identity alone.
measurements: CO amount or formation rate by gas analysis; H2 amount or formation rate by gas analysis; CO/H2 selectivity ratio or fraction with uncertainty across replicates; Total detectable gaseous products covered by the chosen workflow, to avoid selective reporting; Apparent medium descriptor before and after reaction: pH or pD if interpretable in the mixed medium, otherwise conductivity as a bounded proxy; Qualitative phase behavior or precipitation check, because medium change can alter accessibility without proving mechanism
limitations: This card cannot isolate a unique cause because changing water fraction also changes viscosity, conductivity, CO2 solubility, donor protonation, and catalyst/support environment. Even single-factor pairwise contrasts are embedded in a system where effective photon absorption and cobalt speciation may shift with medium. A crossover is therefore strong descriptive evidence for medium involvement but not proof of a specific proton-relay or CO2-adduct mechanism. No claim of matched chemistry should be made from generic donor labels alone.

title: Matched donor comparison with stable bulk descriptors
question: Test whether TEA versus TEOA differences in the P01 Co-bpy/g-C3N4 system reproducibly co-vary with directly measured bulk proton-management and medium descriptors, while keeping the conclusion descriptive rather than causal.
measurements: CO amount or rate under each group; H2 amount or rate under each group; CO/H2 product ratio or selectivity descriptor; Pre-irradiation acidity proxy measured by one calibrated method used consistently across all groups; Post-irradiation acidity proxy shift by the same method; Pre-irradiation conductivity; Post-irradiation conductivity; Replicate-to-replicate variation of catalytic outputs and bulk descriptors
limitations: This card is intentionally narrowed to a descriptive covariate screen. TEA and TEOA may simultaneously alter proton transfer, reductive quenching, coordination, viscosity, and CO2 solvation. Bulk acidity and conductivity do not establish the local environment at active sites, and D2O is not a single-factor perturbation. Therefore the experiment can prioritize which explanations deserve stronger follow-up, but it cannot by itself prove proton-management causation.

title: Operando cobalt-state comparison under TEOA versus TEA
question: Test whether replacing TEOA with TEA in the primary P01 Co-bpy/g-C3N4 CO2-photoreduction formulation changes observable cobalt oxidation-state, coordination, or stability signatures during operation, and whether any donor-dependent state difference tracks catalytic output.
measurements: Co K-edge XANES features versus time, including edge-position and intensity changes if above matrix background; EXAFS-derived coordination-shell trends versus time, reported as model-dependent when multiple fits remain plausible; Complementary UV-vis spectral evolution of the reaction mixture or suspended system under matched sampling state; CO and H2 product amounts or rates from the same runs to test whether spectral differences track catalytic output; No-cobalt background spectra for both TEOA and TEA matrices to identify donor/support/cell contributions; Dark hold-time spectra for each donor as descriptive references rather than operating-state surrogates
limitations: The active cobalt species in P01 is unresolved, and support-associated, solution-phase, and decomposition-derived cobalt species may coexist. Operando XAS is element-specific but cannot by itself prove the catalytic intermediate, isolate donor photochemistry as upstream cause, or exclude decomposition pathways. Complementary UV-vis changes are non-unique and may reflect donor, ligand, support, or scattering effects. Dark comparisons here remain descriptive because irradiation and sampling_mode both differ. Even with paired no-cobalt matrices, assignment should stop at donor-dependent cobalt-linked observables unless independent methods support a narrower claim.

title: TEA versus TEOA pre-irradiation association with Co-bpy formulations
question: Test whether replacing TEOA with TEA changes detectable pre-turnover association or coordination signatures of the Co-bpy formulation, which could predispose different catalytic states before photochemistry begins.
measurements: UV-Vis absorption changes of the precursor mixture as a function of TEA or TEOA addition, including wavelength shifts, new bands, intensity changes, and saturation behavior.; 1H NMR chemical-shift or line-broadening changes for ligand and donor resonances in the simplified homogeneous analogue, with donor-free and amine-only references.; Replicate-to-replicate baseline drift and time-dependent changes in donor-free samples to distinguish true titration responses from precursor instability.; Qualitative sample-state observations such as precipitation or turbidity, because these can signal formulation changes but cannot by themselves establish coordination geometry or active-species identity.
limitations: Most evidence is transferred from other cobalt families or other metals, so any assignment to direct cobalt coordination is provisional. P01 contains g-C3N4, so scattering and heterogeneous interfaces may obscure weak spectral changes. TEA and TEOA also change medium properties, so a spectral difference does not uniquely prove inner-sphere coordination. Conversely, no detectable change does not rule out transient or photoinduced interactions below detection limits. This characterization cannot establish product origin, catalytic necessity, or the identity of the true operating species under illumination.

title: Deactivation and catalyst persistence map
question: Test whether replacing TEOA with TEA changes time-dependent cobalt persistence, donor-dependent state drift, or loss of catalytic output in the primary Co-bpy/g-C3N4 platform, rather than only changing endpoint selectivity.
measurements: Time-resolved CO and H2 amounts from the same analytical method across all groups; these establish output and decay trends but not product origin by themselves.; Cobalt-centered state observables before, during, and after reaction using a transferable method such as XAS or another cobalt-sensitive spectroscopy; these can show donor-dependent valence or coordination changes but may not uniquely identify the active species.; Optional complementary UV-Vis, Raman, or IR signatures on matched samples to detect gross donor-dependent catalyst drift or new species; these are supportive only if assignments are validated.; Mass balance and visible precipitation or phase-change notes to flag catalyst loss or aggregation; these indicate persistence issues but cannot establish molecular identity.; No-cobalt control products and spectra to bound donor/support background contributions and prevent overassignment of donor-derived or support-derived signals to cobalt turnover.
limitations: Direct literature evidence for a strict TEA-versus-TEOA head-to-head in this exact P01 recipe is incomplete. The active cobalt species is unresolved, so state changes may remain descriptive rather than structurally unique. TEA and TEOA can alter donor strength, proton handling, CO2 interaction, viscosity, and coordination simultaneously, so even the primary contrast does not isolate a single causal subfactor. No-cobalt controls bound some background chemistry but do not recreate the full catalytic manifold. Post-reaction characterization alone cannot establish the true operating state.

title: Operando IR/EPR donor-adduct screen
question: Test whether TEA versus TEOA causes different donor-associated cobalt or substrate-bound species under matched P01 conditions, while bounding what any spectral differences can and cannot establish about the CO/H2 shift.
measurements: In situ or near-operando IR difference spectra under CO2 and illumination, tracking donor-dependent new bands, band shifts, and growth or decay behavior relative to dark and donor-free baselines.; In situ or rapid-freeze or rapid-transfer EPR spectra, tracking appearance, disappearance, g-pattern changes, and line broadening under TEA versus TEOA conditions.; Matched catalytic readouts from parallel or same-batch experiments: CO and H2 amounts or rates, reported together rather than selectivity alone.; Background spectra from donor-free, no-cobalt, and dark controls for both donors to establish which signals are not cobalt-specific or not light-dependent.; If signal strength allows, time ordering of spectral changes relative to product formation; this can show correlation but cannot by itself identify the sole active species.
limitations: Assignments are transferred from nonidentical systems and may not map to Co-bpy. IR/EPR can reveal donor-dependent species or state changes but cannot alone establish the full catalytic mechanism, the exact structure of the active cobalt species, or product origin. TEA/TEOA physical-property differences can alter line shape and transport, so apparent spectral differences are not automatically chemical. Near-operando aliquots may miss the true instantaneous working state. No-cobalt controls are background screens, not full single-factor catalytic comparisons because total composition changes.

title: P02 donor-substitution bridge for cobalt-state and quenching readouts
question: Test in the supplementary homogeneous cobalt platform whether replacing TEOA with TEA changes cobalt-state-sensitive observables or donor-coupled quenching behavior under otherwise matched conditions, then compare only the qualitative direction of donor effects to the primary P01 system.
measurements: Steady-state or time-resolved photosensitizer emission quenching versus donor and cobalt presence; this shows relative quenching behavior but cannot by itself identify the full catalytic pathway.; UV-vis spectral changes of the cobalt-containing mixture before and during illumination; these can indicate donor-linked state changes or aggregation but cannot uniquely assign a specific cobalt intermediate without independent confirmation.; If available, operando or near-operando Co K-edge XAS/XANES/EXAFS on matched TEA and TEOA mixtures; these can report average oxidation-state and coordination-environment changes but may miss minority active species.; GC quantification of CO and H2 from the same matched runs; this establishes product distribution changes but not their sole cause.
limitations: Catalyst architecture differs from the Co-bpy/g-C3N4 target, so this is a transfer test rather than a direct explanation of P01. Donor substitution can change medium properties and quenching simultaneously, and homogeneous average-state methods may not reveal minority active species. Cobalt-free blanks help bound but do not eliminate confounding. Spectral changes alone cannot establish exact coordination structures or prove causality for product selectivity.

title: Single-omission matrix for donor-linked cobalt-state effects
question: Test whether any TEA-versus-TEOA difference in cobalt-state observables and CO/H2 distribution requires the full CoCl2+bpy+g-C3N4 assembly, using explicit one-factor omissions and bounded background interpretation.
measurements: CO and H2 quantified together by one matched GC workflow for all groups, reporting amount and CO/H2 distribution.; A cobalt-state observable from an element- or coordination-sensitive method feasible in the laboratory context, such as operando or near-operando XAS, XPS-compatible sampling, or UV-Vis features, with sample state stated explicitly.; Change in cobalt-related spectral features or signal intensity from pre-illumination to illuminated CO2 conditions as a bounded indicator of donor-linked state change or deactivation.; Background product formation in omission groups, used to bound non-full-assembly contributions rather than to claim catalytic equivalence.
limitations: Omission of bpy or g-C3N4 may generate qualitatively different cobalt species rather than partial versions of the full catalyst, so these are dependence tests, not continuity proofs. EV059 does not provide a direct TEA-versus-TEOA head-to-head in one frozen recipe, so baseline comparability still requires verification. Recovered-sample measurements may miss the operating state, and generic spectral changes cannot by themselves identify the active species or exact coordination geometry.

title: CO2-associated speciation versus donor identity before illumination
question: Test whether matched P01 mixtures containing TEA or TEOA show different pre-illumination CO2-associated solution signatures, and whether any donor-dependent signal requires cobalt/bipyridine presence. This addresses the H05 prediction of donor-linked substrate or intermediate association without presuming catalytic relevance.
measurements: IR spectra of pre-illumination mixtures, emphasizing donor- and CO2-dependent new bands or band shifts relative to inert controls; NMR spectra of pre-illumination mixtures, emphasizing donor- and CO2-dependent new resonances, broadening, or chemical-shift changes; Difference spectra between CO2 and inert conditions for each donor condition; Replicate-to-replicate reproducibility of the above signatures under independently prepared matched samples; If phase-separated or clarified aliquots are feasible, comparison of bulk-solution versus suspension-containing signal contributions; this cannot by itself establish catalytic on-pathway relevance or exact structure
limitations: This experiment is characterization only and cannot establish that any detected species lies on the catalytic pathway or controls CO/H2 selectivity. TEA/TEOA change multiple chemical properties beyond simple donor strength, so donor identity is a bundled factor even in the single-factor contrast. Because cobalt, bpy, and g-C3N4 remain present in all main groups, any observed signal may arise from bulk amine-CO2 chemistry, catalyst-linked adducts, support-associated species, or combinations thereof. Pre-illumination measurements may miss the operating photochemical state.

title: Operando isotope-sensitive IR for TEA versus TEOA
question: Test whether donor identity changes reaction-state IR features consistent with CO2-associated or hydrogen-involving species in the P01 Co-bpy context, using symmetric isotope and negative controls so any TEA-versus-TEOA difference is bounded in both donor conditions rather than inferred from products alone.
measurements: Time-resolved IR spectra under illumination for all groups.; Wavenumber positions, isotope shifts, and temporal evolution of donor-dependent bands under TEA and TEOA.; Presence or absence of candidate bands in cobalt-present versus cobalt-absent references for each donor.; Symmetry of 13CO2 and D2O assignment behavior across TEA and TEOA conditions.; Signal-to-noise, baseline stability, repeatability across replicate runs, and degree of band overlap.
limitations: Evidence is transferred from non-Co systems and general methods. Band assignment may remain ambiguous because donor, solvent, bicarbonate or carbonate, products, and cobalt-ligand features can overlap. Isotope substitution can alter kinetics as well as frequencies. Near-operando spectra may miss the true operating state, and operando IR alone cannot prove the primary quenching route, exact adduct identity, or whether a detected species is on-path rather than spectator. Cobalt-absent controls bound background contributions but do not separately isolate all non-cobalt components.

title: 13CO2-bounded TEA versus TEOA benchmark with matched background controls
question: Test whether any TEA/TEOA difference in apparent CO/H2 selectivity remains when counted CO is explicitly confirmed as CO2-derived within the P01 Co-bpy comparison, while checking donor-dependent background gas formation under no-CO2 and dark conditions.
measurements: Headspace CO isotopologue signals distinguishing 13CO from unlabeled/background CO; Total CO amount together with isotopic fraction assigned as CO2-derived; H2 amount measured in the same samples; CO/H2 ratio and 13CO/H2 ratio under matched conditions; Dark-control and inert-gas-control gas outputs as background bounds; Replicate-to-replicate consistency of gas analysis and isotopic assignment
limitations: This candidate bounds carbon origin but does not directly observe amine-CO2 adducts, catalyst-linked intermediates, or operating cobalt speciation. TEA and TEOA can change multiple hidden properties even when nominal formulation is matched, including proton activity and solvation, so a donor effect here is not uniquely attributable to adduct stabilization. The dark control is intentionally limited and, if only one donor is used, becomes a multi-factor descriptive check rather than a donor-specific contrast. Transfer from the cited literature is methodological and cautionary, not direct proof for P01.

title: TEA/TEOA matched catalytic readout with inert-gas, negative controls, and optional isotope follow-up
question: Test whether any TEA-versus-TEOA difference in CO/H2 distribution persists after tighter matching plus core controls, while limiting inference to a bounded donor comparison unless a platform-qualified substrate-associated signal is first established.
measurements: CO and H2 quantified together by one unchanged analytical method across all groups; Predefined quenching observable for the platform, such as emission quenching or excited-state decay of the light-absorbing component; If pilot-qualified, one substrate-associated or intermediate-associated spectral feature collected with matched blanks and backgrounds; For optional 13CO2 groups, isotopic product assignment if detectable; Covariates affecting comparability, including pH or apparent basicity proxy, optical density, visible precipitation, and color change; Replicate-to-replicate variability and practical detection limits for each readout
limitations: The card remains a staged discriminator because the supplied record does not establish a validated substrate-associated signal in the target platform. TEA and TEOA can alter several medium properties beyond donor identity, so even the primary donor contrast may combine donor, base, proton-management, and solvation effects. Inert-gas, no-cobalt, dark, and 13CO2 controls improve assignment but do not identify the exact active intermediate or prove a productive donor-catalyst adduct.

title: Amine omission and TEA versus TEOA contrast under matched CO2 exposure
question: Test whether donor presence is necessary for any CO2-associated spectroscopic signature and whether TEOA gives a donor-identity-specific signature or product-origin pattern beyond a generic amine effect in the P01 Co-bpy context.
measurements: Gas-phase CO and H2 from each group; if 13CO2 is used, isotopic composition of CO when detectable.; Operando or near-operando IR, Raman, UV-Vis, XAS, or other validated speciation signal selected by pilot for sensitivity to donor-dependent CO2-associated or catalyst-associated changes.; Pre-illumination versus illuminated spectra under matched backgrounds to distinguish pre-equilibrated adduct formation from light-dependent changes.; Medium covariates needed for comparability, such as pH or other donor-induced bulk changes, noting that these covariates do not establish identical local chemistry.; If a donor-specific spectroscopic feature appears, its presence or absence across groups; the signal can indicate association or state change but cannot alone prove a complete catalytic pathway or exact structure without independent assignment support.
limitations: TEA and TEOA differ simultaneously in donor, base, coordination, and medium effects, so even a single-factor formulation change does not isolate one microscopic cause. Cross-system literature on Re or other catalysts motivates but does not prove analogous Co-bpy adducts. No-amine controls may strongly suppress catalysis, limiting comparison to necessity rather than selectivity. Spectroscopic assignments may be ambiguous without orthogonal confirmation, and recovered-sample measurements may miss the operating state.

title: Symmetric cobalt-linked adduct screen
question: Screen whether TEA versus TEOA under matched P01 conditions gives donor-specific operando substrate-associated signals that are cobalt-dependent and CO2-origin-bounded on both donor sides, while limiting conclusions to descriptive donor-linked differences unless orthogonal assignment succeeds.
measurements: Operando IR features in regions plausibly associated with CO2-derived, carbonate-like, bicarbonate-like, amine-associated, or metal-associated species, interpreted only against matched no-cobalt, dark, and isotope controls.; One preselected cobalt-sensitive operando observable indicating donor-correlated changes in cobalt oxidation state or coordination environment; useful for state comparison but insufficient alone for intermediate assignment.; Feature persistence or loss in no-cobalt controls to distinguish catalyst-linked behavior from donor/background bands.; Feature persistence or loss in dark controls to distinguish operating-state signals from dark pre-equilibria.; Isotope-sensitive shifts or non-shifts in selected donor-specific features under 13CO2 to bound CO2-derived character on both donor sides.
limitations: Direct Co-bpy evidence for TEA/TEOA adduct chemistry is absent in the supplied record. Heterogeneous background from g-C3N4 and mixed media may obscure weak bands. Even symmetric isotope controls do not cleanly distinguish amine-linked from cobalt-linked CO2-derived structures. No-cobalt controls alter the coordination environment, so they support but do not prove catalyst-linked assignment.
